rationale: Solver-validation cases for compliant box-box (cuboid-cuboid) contact (Q76), on neutral fixtures. Values are solver-validation parameters, not material or Kin-candidate claims. Results are labeled fixture and qualify only box-box contact within the declared conditions. Every numeric value is either copied from criteria/fixture-validation/analytic-v1.json (status copied, field named in source) or labeled provisional with its basis. Where a case is the block-on-block analogue of an analytic-v1 case, the analytic-v1 tolerance is copied unchanged (Q76 section 5). Tolerance principles follow docs/decisions/Q048-fixture-validation-reference-conditions.md. This file changes no existing criterion.

gravity.source: Copied from analytic-v1 gravity. Tabletop is the world plane z = 0. Overridden per case only where a case says so: BB7 rotates the direction, BB8 sets the magnitude to 0.

friction_grid_source: Copied verbatim from analytic-v1 friction_grid. One pair is applied to every contact in a run: table-body and body-body.

fixtures.pose: centre (0, 0, 0.01) m, axis-aligned, resting on the tabletop plane z = 0 unless a case says otherwise
fixtures.basis: Added by this file. Q76 names a static block under the dynamic one in BB2 to BB5, but the 40 mm flat block is shorter than the analytic-v1 sliding travel (stop distance 0.064 m at mu_low; above-threshold travel of 0.2 m or more) so the moving block would leave its support. The slab is larger in plan only; its 20 mm thickness equals the flat block. A static body has no mass in the solver. It is a solver fixture, never a Kin candidate (Q38).

duration_s.source: analytic-v1 protocol revision 2 settle (docs/validation/fixture-analytic-v1-protocol.md); not a criteria field

settle.applies_to: every dynamic body that starts in contact, in BB1 to BB5 and BB7
settle.note: Bodies start exactly touching, aligned, at rest, and settle under gravity with no validation load for this long. t = 0 starts after settling. BB4 and BB8 and BB6 are not settled.

poses.orientation: identity (axis-aligned), both centred on the same vertical line

metrics.tangential_force_reference: weight carried by the interface under test
metrics.penetration_applies_to: every interface (table-bottom, bottom-top), max over the whole run

newton_third_law_rel_tol.basis: the bottom-top impulse is applied equal and opposite to both bodies (Q76 section 2), so the two bodies' reported contact forces differ only by rounding; double-precision margin like BB6/BB7

duration_s.basis: analytic-v1 uses 1.0 s. At 1.1x mu_static the block accelerates at up to 2.84 m/s2 (mu_high), so over 1.0 s it would leave the 0.6 m slab (CoM travel 1.42 m). At 0.4 s the largest CoM travel is 0.23 m, inside the slab half-length of 0.3 m less the block half-width

accel_window_start_s.basis: analytic-v1 uses 0.5 of 1.0 s (half the run); half of the shortened run, with the block already sliding at the kinetic coefficient

stays_on_slab.basis: validity check: the top-block CoM horizontal position stays within the slab footprint shrunk by the block half-width, else the run is invalid and fails

BB3.stop_point: bottom-face centre of the top block (analytic-v1 protocol revision 2 definition)

stays_on_slab.basis: validity check as in BB2 above; the largest stop distance is 0.064 m (mu_low), far inside the slab

BB4.settle: none (the block is released from rest at the stated clearance)

duration_s.basis: same total length as BB1 (copied rest.duration_s value 2.0); the impact happens at about 0.14 s and the rest-state window then starts well after the contact transient has damped

max_penetration_m.basis: impact penetration is dynamic, so the 1e-4 m rest bound (analytic-v1 rest.max_penetration_m) does not apply. Undamped bound from energy balance at the impact speed v = sqrt(2 g 0.1) = 1.4 m/s: x = v * sqrt(m / (4 k)) = 4.4e-4 m with four contacts at k = 1e5 N/m, m = 0.04 kg. The limit is that bound rounded up by a factor of about two, and is still 5 percent of the 20 mm block thickness

peak_penetration.rest_penetration_window: max over the rest window only

no_contact_before_clearance_closes.basis: any normal force before the bottom face first reaches the slab top (separation <= 0) fails the case, as free_fall.contact in analytic-v1 does

no_tunnelling.basis: the top-block CoM height never falls below slab top + half the block thickness - the peak penetration limit

BB5.threshold_force: top_mass_kg * g * 0.01 / 0.05 (moment about the +x bottom edge; lever 0.05 m above the pivot, weight arm 0.01 m)
BB5.threshold_note: identical to the analytic-v1 tipping threshold because the support surface, friction law and fixture are the same; mu_low (0.3) exceeds the 0.2 threshold ratio so the block pivots rather than slides at every pair
BB5.pivot_point: the +x bottom-edge midpoint of the top block (analytic-v1 definition)

BB6.friction_and_timestep: not applicable. Evaluated once, with no integration
BB6.run_label_note: the contact generator is called directly on the stated poses; no step is taken

position_depth_rel_tol.basis: Q76 section 5: double-precision margin. Relative to max(|expected|, position_scale_m)

position_scale_m.basis: largest fixture dimension; lets the relative tolerance apply to coordinates whose expected value is zero

normal_component_abs_tol.basis: Q76 section 5: unit vector, so absolute and relative coincide

BB6.pair_order: (A, B); the contact normal points from A to B; reported point and depth as stated per configuration

swap_check.basis: Q79: each configuration is also run with (B, A). Expected: normal negated, same depth, same point count, and each swapped point equal to the corresponding (A, B) point translated by depth along the (A, B) normal, i.e. on the other box's face, since the reported point lies on the incident face and swapping exchanges the incident box. v1 said 'same point set', which contradicts the incident-face rule by one depth (run 1, 2d4dd12).

BB6.point_comparison: point sets compared after sorting by (x, y, z); count must equal exactly; feature ids must be strictly increasing with no duplicates

configurations.expected_axis: A local z (SAT axis index 2). Axis 5 (B local z) ties; the fixed order picks the lower index
configurations.points_on: incident face (B bottom face plane z = 0.0095): the overlap rectangle x in [-0.005, 0.02], y in [-0.01, 0.02]

B.orientation_note: x' = x cos + z sin, z' = -x sin + z cos with theta = 45 degrees; matrix entries are sqrt(0.5)

configurations.lowest_edge_of_B: along y at x = 0.012071067811865, z = 0.0095; spans y in [-0.015, 0.025], clipped to A top face y <= 0.02
configurations.expected_axis: A local z (SAT axis 2). Axis 7 (A local x cross B local y = world z) ties with it and loses by order
configurations.incident_face_tie: the two faces of B that meet at the lowest edge have equal anti-parallelism to the normal (45 degrees); the lower B face index is used. Both give the same two points

A.orientation_note: y' = y cos - z sin, z' = y sin + z cos with theta = 45 degrees

edges.crossing: at right angles in plan, at (0.007071067811865, 0.007071067811865), inside both edge extents

configurations.expected_axis: edge pair A local x with B local y (SAT axis index 7); every face axis has overlap of at least 9.4e-3 m, far above 5e-4 m
configurations.expected_point_definition: midpoint of the two closest edge points: z = (0.021213203435596 + 0.020713203435596) / 2

scenes.base: top flat block resting on the static slab, as BB2/BB3 poses, no validation load; evaluated as the BB1 rest case with the slab as the bottom body
BB3 slide to stop on the slab

BB7.base_note: The tabletop plane z = 0 is world-fixed in the solver and cannot be rotated. Both scenes therefore contain no table contact: the slab and the dynamic block are both lifted off the table by the translation below, and the table never touches them

transform.rotation_definition: rotation by an angle with cosine 0.8 and sine 0.6 about the unit axis (1, 2, 2) / 3; the matrix is orthonormal exactly in rational arithmetic
transform.applied_to: every body position and orientation (R times the body rotation), every initial velocity (R v), the gravity direction, and the applied slide direction

minimum_table_clearance_m.basis: the scene extent is below 0.7 m about its origin, so with z shifted by 5 m every point stays at least 4 m above the tabletop plane

BB7.comparison: each scene is run twice, identity and transformed, at the same (friction pair, timestep). Body-relative quantities are compared

S1: centre of pressure in the top block frame
top block rotation angle relative to the slab (the quaternion relative to the slab, as an angle)
top block CoM displacement in the slab frame
S3: stop distance along the slide direction
post-stop drift in the slab frame

rel_tol.basis: Q76 s5 said 1e-9; lead review before registration raised it: a rotated scene is not bit-identical in IEEE 754, and stick-slip over 1000+ steps can amplify rounding. 1e-6 is still 100x tighter than the physics tolerances (1e-4 m penetration, 1e-3 relative force), so a real frame dependence fails. Relative to max(|reference|, scale), scale 1 N, 0.04 m, 1 rad, 1 s

abs_floor.basis: avoids dividing by zero for quantities that are exactly zero in the reference; same order as the coupler audits' absolute floors

stop_step_index_tol.basis: rounding can move the speed threshold crossing by one step; a frame dependence larger than one step fails

gravity_override.basis: gravity disabled for this case only, so momentum is conserved with no external force

initial_gap_m.basis: gap between the facing faces at t = 0 (B bottom face z = 0.011, A top face z = 0.010); small enough that contact occurs within the first 0.01 s and large enough not to start in contact

offset_x_m.basis: B is offset from A by 10 mm in x so the normal impulse is eccentric and both bodies spin about y; the spin axis is a principal axis of the flat block (gyroscopic term omitted by the analytic protocol therefore does not change angular momentum)

duration_s.basis: B moves 0.15 m in x, which clears the 0.04 m width of A so the last sample is contact-free

min_peak_tangential_impulse_n_s.basis: far above rounding, far below the expected friction impulse of order 1e-3 N s (mu_low x about 2e-3): a run with no friction activity did not exercise sliding contact and fails

sliding_engaged.basis: Relative tangential speed 0.3 m/s against a reduced-mass normal impulse scale of 2e-3 N s makes sliding the expected regime at every friction pair (m_r * v_t = 6e-3 N s exceeds mu_static * about 4e-3 N s)

final_sample_contact_free.basis: precondition: the final sample has no body pair overlap (SAT separation > 0). If it does, the energy audit is not valid and the run fails

momentum.form: max over t > 0 of |p - p0| / (rel_tol_of_m_g_t * M * g_n * t + abs_floor_kg_m_s), limit <= 1
momentum.M: sum of the two body masses
momentum.g_n: the standard gravity constant 9.80665 m/s2 used as a scale even though the applied gravity is 0, so the allowance keeps the coupler form (the reference p0 + M g t reduces to p0)
momentum.note: the coupler form has the term (M g t); with gravity applied it is the momentum change gravity can explain. Here it is used only as a scale for the rounding allowance

angular_momentum.form: max over t > 0 of |L - L0| / (rel_tol * M * g_n * t * r_ref + abs_floor_kg_m2_s), limit <= 1
angular_momentum.about: the world origin, L = sum over bodies of (r_c x m v + R I_body R^T omega)

rel_tol.basis: same relative tolerance as the linear momentum audit

abs_floor_kg_m2_s.basis: same order as the linear floor

impulse_accounting.definition: for every step, each body's change in linear momentum equals the sum of the contact impulses the solver reports for that body, within the allowance

energy.quantity: kinetic energy of both bodies, translational plus rotational, total; no stored potential exists because gravity is off and both the first and last samples are contact-free
energy.creation_rule: E_final <= E_0 + (creation_rel_tol + first_order_omega_dt_coefficient * omega_ref * dt) * E_0 + abs_floor_j

first_order_omega_dt_coefficient.basis: the coupler value 1.0 compensates the shadow energy of stored potential in the final sample (Q60 section 1). Here both evaluated samples are contact-free, so no potential is stored in either and the term does not apply. If the final sample were in contact the run would already fail the final_sample_contact_free precondition. A larger omega_ref * dt term would also make this audit vacuous at these stiffnesses (sqrt(4k/m_r) = 4.5e3 rad/s)

energy.omega_ref_definition: sqrt(4 * contact_stiffness / m_reduced), reported as informational for the audit record
energy.dissipation_reported: E_0 - E_final reported, informational, not gated (the compliant damping legitimately dissipates)

requirement.basis: as the coupler C9 requirement: an audit that cannot detect an unmodeled velocity change is not evidence of conservation. Controls are applied in the evaluator on a copy of the trace, not in the solver

scope.value: every run of BB1 to BB5, BB7 (identity and transformed) and BB8 at every (friction pair, timestep) combination is executed twice from the same configuration and the canonical final-state hashes compared; BB6 is repeated and its full output compared bitwise
scope.basis: Q76 says only bit-identical final-state hashes; the cases to which it applies are made explicit here
